---
title: "Universal eye-movement experiments with OpenSesame and PyGaze"
format: revealjs
---

## Goals

- Write one experiment that runs on **any PyGaze-supported eye tracker**
- Develop and test with the PyGaze **advanced dummy** tracker (mouse = gaze)
- Four experiments: reading, boundary (display change), moving window, visual world

## Setup

```bash
docker pull bangele1/opensesame-test-container
docker run -it -v $PWD:/work bangele1/opensesame-test-container
cd /work/experiments && python reading.py
```

Set `TRACKERTYPE=eyelink` (or `tobii`, `eyetribe`, ...) to switch hardware; the default `dummy` is the advanced dummy.

## PyGaze building blocks

```python
disp = libscreen.Display(); kb = libinput.Keyboard()
tracker = eyetracker.EyeTracker(disp, trackertype="dummy")
tracker.calibrate()
tracker.start_recording(); tracker.log("MSG"); tracker.stop_recording()
x, y = tracker.sample()
```

All shared code lives in `experiments/common.py`. The same code can be pasted into OpenSesame `inline_script` items.

## Experiment 1: reading (`reading.py`)

- Sentences from `stimuli/reading.csv`, one per trial
- Drift check → start recording → show sentence → log `STIMONSET` → key press ends trial
- Based on the sampling-rate revision study

## Experiment 2: boundary paradigm (`boundary.py`)

- Preview string shown in the target position
- Poll `tracker.sample()`; when gaze passes the invisible boundary, swap to the target word
- Log `DISPLAYCHANGE` so change latency can be analysed

```python
if gaze_x(tracker) > boundary:
    disp.fill(tar_scr); disp.show()
```

## Experiment 3: moving window (`movingwindow.py`)

- Only characters within *window* characters of gaze are visible; others become `x`
- Screen redrawn whenever the fixated character changes
- Window size is a column in `stimuli/movingwindow.csv`

## Experiment 4: visual world (`vwp.py`)

- Four objects in quadrants (drop `<name>.png` files into `stimuli/`)
- Instruction presented; gaze samples per region counted and logged
- Swap the on-screen text for an audio sampler in OpenSesame for real spoken stimuli

## Analysis

Logs are tracker-native (dummy: tab-separated text) and contain `TRIALSTART`, `STIMONSET`,
`DISPLAYCHANGE`, `WINDOWMOVE`, `SAMPLES` messages. Use R (`readr`) or Python (`pandas`) to compute fixation durations and fixation proportions.

## Next steps

- Real hardware: change `TRACKERTYPE`, recalibrate
- Check display-change timing with a photodiode
